headline: A weak, fizzling storm brings breezy winds and only light snow north of Lake Tahoe Tuesday night into Wednesday, leaving Mammoth Lakes and the rest of the eastern Sierra south of Tahoe mostly dry, before calm, dry and increasingly mild weather takes over for Thanksgiving and the weekend.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: After a cold morning with patches of freezing fog, Monday afternoon and Monday night stay dry around Mammoth Lakes and across the region, with light breezes. Mid- and high-level clouds increase from the afternoon on ahead of a weak approaching storm.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Tuesday is dry and a few degrees milder as high pressure passes through, with highs in the upper 30s to mid 40s for eastern Sierra communities like Mammoth Lakes and northeast California, and mid 40s to low 50s in the western Nevada valleys. A weak storm that looks less impressive with each model run moves through Tuesday night into Wednesday morning: very little or no precipitation is expected south of Lake Tahoe, including Mammoth Lakes, or in western Nevada. North of Tahoe, totals are generally 0.10 inch or less, with the most (0.10–0.15 inch) around Lassen Volcanic National Park and only a trace to 1 inch of snow above 6,500 feet there; western Lassen County has a 10–20 percent chance of light rain or snow by late Tuesday evening. Southwest winds pick up Tuesday afternoon from Tahoe northward, with bumpy flying conditions over the mountains and around Reno into Tuesday night and a 15 percent chance of light snow showers lowering visibility around Truckee and South Lake Tahoe.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: From late Wednesday into the weekend, high pressure builds over the West, bringing calm, dry weather, with temperatures back to normal by Thanksgiving and above normal into the weekend. Under that high pressure, cold air will get trapped in the valleys each night, with temperature inversions (cold, stagnant air near the ground under warmer air) strengthening into the weekend. Computer models suggest a more active, stormy pattern could set up Sunday into early next week, but rain, mountain snow and wind details are very uncertain.

watch_for: Breezy southwest winds and light snow showers north of Lake Tahoe Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, with a small chance of reduced visibility near Truckee and South Lake Tahoe.
Strengthening valley inversions (trapped cold, stagnant air) from Thanksgiving into the weekend.
A possibly stormier pattern Sunday into next week, with rain, mountain snow and wind details still uncertain.
confidence: Forecasters are confident the midweek storm will be weak and that Thanksgiving through Saturday will be dry and mild, and have low confidence in the details of a possibly stormy pattern starting Sunday.
